chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who intended to emancipate a slave of his, and his master used to take a tax from him that he had obligated upon him every year, and the master was pleased with that from him, and the slave was pleased with that. So the slave acquired wealth in his trade besides what he used to give his master from the tax. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he pays to his master what was obligated upon him, then whatever he earns after the obligation, it is for the slave.'

He said, then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that Allah has obligated obligations upon the servants, so when they fulfill them to Him, He does not ask them about what is besides it?' So I said to him: 'So the slave may give charity from what he earns and emancipate [others] after the obligation which he used to pay to his master?' He said: 'Yes, and the reward of that is for him.'

I said: 'So if he emancipates a slave from what he had earned besides the obligation, to whom will belong the guardianship of the emancipated one?' He said: 'He goes and gives guardianship to whomever he likes. If he guarantees his crimes and his wergild, he will be his master and inherit him.' I said: 'Is it not that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates?'' He said: 'This is a Sa'iba [unconditionally freed slave], his guardianship cannot be for a slave like him.'

I said: 'So if the slave who emancipates him guarantees his crimes and his liabilities, will that necessitate it and he will become his master and inherit him?' He said: 'That is not allowed, and a slave does not inherit a free one.'

key_terms.وَلَاء: Guardianship or right of inheritance upon emancipation

ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights of a slave who pays a fixed annual tax to his master, and who inherits the emancipated slave?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) draws a parallel between the slave’s financial autonomy and the believer’s relationship with Allah, noting that just as God does not demand beyond the obligatory duties, the master has no claim over the slave's surplus earnings. The narration further refines the concept of *walā'* (lineage/guardianship), distinguishing between the general rule that 'freedom follows the one who frees' and the specific case of *Sa'iba*, where the emancipator retains rights only if they guarantee the freed slave's blood money and liabilities, a nuance highlighted by the Imam's clarification that a slave cannot inherit a free person.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who intended to emancipate a slave of his, and his master used to take tax from him obligated upon him during every year, and the master was happy with that and the slave was happy with that. So the slave attained wealth in his business equal to what he was giving to his master from the taxes. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he pays to his master what was obligated upon him, so whatever he earns after the obligation, so it is for the slave’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it not the case that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Obligated certain Obligations upon the servant, so when he fulfils it, He<sup>asws</sup> would not Ask him about what is besides it?’ So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So it is for the slave that he gives in charity from what he earns, and he emancipates after the obligation which was payable to his master?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and the Recompense of that is for him’.

I said, ‘So if he emancipates a slave from what he had earned, besides the obligation, to whom would belong the guardianship of the emancipated one?’ Heasws said: ‘He should go and give the guardianship to the one whom he likes, who would take the responsibility of his crimes and wergild, he would be his guardian and his inheritor’. I said, ‘Is it not the case that Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The guardianship is for the one who emancipates?’ Heasws said: ‘This is a Sa’iba (an unconditionally freed slave), his guardianship cannot happen to be for a slave like him’.

I said, ‘So if the slave who emancipate guarantees the responsibility of his crimes, and his liabilities, would that necessitate and he would become his master and inherit him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not allowed, and a slave would not inherit a free one’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from af-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who wants to free his slave. His master takes a certain amount of tax from him every year about which both the master and slave had happily agreed. The slave in business earns a certain amount of assets besides what he gives to his master as tax. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he pays to his master what was obligatory, thereafter what he earns belongs to the slave.’

He (the Imam) then said, Ts it not the case that Allah has made certain things obligatory on His servants and when they fulfill such obligations, He then does not ask for more?’ I then asked, ‘Can the slave give charity out of what he earns and set free after paying his dues to his master? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so and the reward for it belongs to him.’

I then asked, ‘If he frees a slave with his earning which is other than his dues, with whom then rests guardianship because of setting him free? He (the Imam) said, ‘He can go and find guardians that he likes. Whoever bails out his crimes and wergild such person becomes his guardian and heir.’ I then asked, ‘1s not it the case that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “Guardianship rests with the one who buys one’s freedom?”’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave). Guardianship over him will not rest with another slave like him.’

I then asked, ‘If the slave that he has freed guarantees and bails out his crime and liabilities, does it become binding and because of this becomes his guardian and inherits him? He (the Imam) said, ‘That is not permissible because a slave cannot inherit one who is free.’”
